page.layout: One column of running text, centred on the page. Running head at top right: "De Duellis." with page number 305. No marginal notes. Catchword "rum" at the foot, right-aligned below the last line. The faint text in the lower right corner is a digitiser's mark and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: possit, etiam assequatur. Participem enim esse discipulum afflictionum sui magistri, quid aliud est, quam velle una cum magistro ejusdem conditionis esse participem. Ut patienter quemq; ferre oporteat contumelias, & injurias sibimet illatas, vindictam Deo committendo, uti ipse Christus suas æquo animo pertulit, nec eas ulcisci voluit. Et uti non est infamiâ notandus miles, qui quæ peragit, mandato ducis peragit. Nec ignominiæ notam subditus incurrit, qui sui principis edicta tuetur. Ita nec turpitudinis maculâ aspergitur, qui renuit conditionem duelli quia Salvator noster, dux noster mandat, jubet, ferendas esse injurias, ac differendas, malumque illatum bono esse rependendum. Ipse securus omnium, Deo patri vindictam injuriarum illata-rum

page.notes: The catchword "rum" completes "illatarum" on the next page. The page is a single paragraph, since no line is indented and no paragraph break is printed. Some letters are damaged by the scan (for example "repellendum" in the last lines, which I read as "rependendum"). Light marks on the left and right margins are show-through or noise and are not transcribed.
